newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL GREATS CLASH AT SOUTHAMPTON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL GREATS CLASH AT SOUTHAMPTON.

text.p: Two Liverpool greats cross swords at Southampton on Saturday while a third, Kevin Keegan, will be there in spirit.

Kenny Dalglish, who stepped into Keegan's shoes at St James's Park on Tuesday, takes his first Newcastle side to the Dell, where Keegan was once a player and where his former Liverpool team mate Graeme Souness is now manager.
Scottish duo Dalglish and Souness were at the hub of the mighty Liverpool side which lifted the European Cup three times between 1977 and 1981 and dominated English soccer for a decade.
Both went on to manage Liverpool, Souness with little success, Dalglish leading them to three league titles in 1986, 1988 and 1990.
And the links in the intriguing Liverpool-Southampton-Newcastle chain do not end there.
When Dalglish steps out at the Dell he will find himself in one of Keegan's old haunts -- Keegan played at Southampton from 1980 to 82 before moving to Newcastle.

It was Dalglish who took over the number seven shirt at Liverpool when Keegan left Anfield in 1977, and it is Dalglish who now has the task of building on the foundations laid by Keegan at Newcastle in his five years as manager.
In addition, Saturday's clash holds special meaning for Dalglish's prize asset at Newcastle, England striker Alan Shearer, and assistant manager Terry McDermott.
Shearer is returning to the ground where he started his career before joining Dalglish at Blackburn. McDermott is another of the great names from the Liverpool of the late 1970s and 1980s.
All that past shared history will be concentrated in the cramped Southampton stadium as Newcastle look to start the Dalglish era in style.

They were unconvincing in their 2-1 F.A. Cup win over Charlton in midweek and have a number of injury worries, most notably to Belgian defender Philippe Albert, who limped out of that match with a hamstring strain.
"Albert's injury is not as bad as we first thought but I don't think he will be in contention for tomorrow," Dalglish said.
Steve Watson, who suffered a heel injury against Charlton, travels with the squad but is another doubtful starter.
"There are three or four others who have picked up some bumps and bruises as well so we will have to see what our numbers are after (Friday) training," Dalglish said.
If Watson does play, he will probably take Albert's place at centre-back with Warren Barton, who came on as a substitute against Charlton, replacing Watson at right-back.
Rob Lee returns after a two-match suspension and Shearer's strike partner Les Ferdinand, who has been carrying an ankle injury, is fit.
England midfielder Matt Le Tissier is set to return for Southampton after being left on the substitutes' bench for last weekend's game 1-0 win at Middlesbrough.
Centre-back Richard Dryden may replace suspended defender Francis Benali after recovering from a hamstring injury which has ruled him out for the last four weeks.
One thing appears certain. The Newcastle players have every confidence in their new manager.
"You wouldn't think anyone could step into Kevin Keegan's shoes but if there's one man on earth who can it's Kenny Dalglish," goalkeeper Shaka Hislop said.
